Simulating many diffusions

Source: R/model_diffusion.R, R/report_models.R
play_diffusions.Rd

play_diffusions() runs manynet::play_diffusion() times times on the same network, and binds the reports of every run into one diffs_model. Give the result to test_gof(), to compare an observed diffusion with it, or to test_distributions(), to compare it with another model.

Runs in which nothing spreads beyond the seeds return no report from manynet::as_diffusion(), and are dropped with a warning.

Usage

play_diffusions(.data, ..., times = 5, control = list())

# S3 method for class 'diffs_model'
summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'diffs_model'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

.data

A network of a manynet-consistent class, such as a matrix, an edgelist, an igraph, a network, a tbl_graph, or a stocnet object.

...

Arguments passed on to manynet::play_diffusion(), such as transmissibility, recovery, or steps.

times

The number of diffusions to simulate. By default 5, but 1,000-10,000 simulations are recommended for a test.

control

The controls of the simulations, as the result of control_mrqap() or a named list of its arguments, such as list(ncores = 4, seed = 1). It reads ncores, strategy, and seed, and leaves the other controls alone. The same seed gives the same diffusions sequentially and in parallel. A control that is not named keeps its default, or the value set with control_mrqap(..., persist = TRUE). The result records the controls that it used in its attribute control.

object, x

A diffs_model.

Value

A diffs_model: a tibble with one row for each step of each run, the run in sim, the step in time, and the counts of manynet::as_diffusion(). summary() gives the time of adoption, the number of steps until every node is infected, for each run. print() returns x, invisibly.

Details

print() shows a title that says how many diffusions were simulated, the report of each step, and a footer with the steps until every node adopted. summary() gives those steps for each simulation.

See also

Other models: control_mrqap(), diagnose_confusion(), other_results, print.netreg_lm(), regression, specify, specify_terms, terms_mrqap, test_fit, test_measures, test_parameter()

Examples

play_diffusions(ison_adolescents, transmissibility = 0.3, times = 5,
                control = list(seed = 1))
#> # 5 simulated SI diffusions
#> 
#> # A tibble: 38 × 6
#>      sim  time     n     S     s     I
#>    <int> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <int>
#>  1     1     0     8     7     1     1
#>  2     1     1     8     7     1     1
#>  3     1     2     8     6     3     2
#>  4     1     3     8     4     3     4
#>  5     1     4     8     3     2     5
#>  6     1     5     8     2     1     6
#>  7     2     0     8     7     1     1
#>  8     2     1     8     7     1     1
#>  9     2     2     8     6     3     2
#> 10     2     3     8     6     3     2
#> # ℹ 28 more rows
#> 
#> # Steps until every node adopted: median 9, from 7 to 10.
#> # Controls: seed = 1
